The first release of Zeval: a UCI chess engine written entirely in x86-64 assembly, with a classical tapered evaluation. In loving memory of my father.

## Downloads

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `zeval-1.0-windows-x64.zip` | `zeval.exe` for 64-bit Windows 10 / 11 (imports only `KERNEL32.dll`, no runtime to install) |
| `zeval-1.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `zeval` for x86-64 Linux (static, no libc) |
| `zeval-1.0-testkit-windows.zip` | prebuilt test and candidate builds for `verify_smp.bat`, `verify_units.bat` and `sprt_candidate.bat`: unpack into the root of a checkout of this tag |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | SHA-256 of the archives and of both engine binaries |

Add the executable to any UCI GUI or tournament manager (Arena, Cute Chess, fastchess, cutechess-cli, Lucas Chess and others). Started without a GUI it plays in the terminal.

## Highlights

- Principal Variation Search with a lock-free transposition table, null-move pruning, razoring, reverse futility and futility pruning, late move reductions, SEE ordering and pruning, check and singular extensions.
- Lazy SMP with up to 32 threads: persistent helper threads, best-move vote over all threads.
- Time management that spreads the clock over the game and adapts to the stability of the best move and the score.
- Classical evaluation: mobility, pawn structure, passed pawns, king safety, threats, an endgame scale factor and special endgame knowledge (KPK bitbase, KBNK, KQ-KR, KR-KB, KR-KN).
- UCI options: `Hash` (up to 32 GB), `Clear Hash`, `Threads` (1 to 32), `Move Overhead`.

## Verifying the download

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing
```

The executables are built by the release workflow of this repository from the tagged source; `build/build.sh` links reproducibly, so a build with the same toolchain (NASM 2.16, LLD 18) gives the same files.

## Known limitations

No endgame tablebases, no MultiPV, no `Ponder` option, no opening book. The Windows executable is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may show an "unknown publisher" warning.
